stem: A reconciliation job compares two result sets of identical shape and has to return only the records present on both sides. Duplicate records must not survive into the output, and the team would rather not write a join for this.

option_texts.A: INTERSECT, which returns the set of rows which are in both subqueries
option_texts.B: UNION, which combines both sides and keeps each record once
option_texts.C: EXCEPT, which keeps the records of the first side that the second lacks
option_texts.D: UNION ALL, which stacks both sides and leaves every record in place

drill_answer_short: INTERSECT returns the rows present in both subqueries, and DISTINCT is its default
decision_hinge: INTERSECT returns the set of rows which are in both subqueries, and if DISTINCT is specified the result does not contain any duplicate rows, which is the default.

plausible_options.B: return only the records present on both sides

eliminated_by.C: compares two result sets of identical shape
eliminated_by.D: Duplicate records must not survive into the output

distractor_traps.B: T3: confusable sibling - UNION merges both sides rather than keeping only the overlap
distractor_traps.C: T3: confusable sibling - EXCEPT is the complement, returning what the second side lacks
distractor_traps.D: T5: common misconception - ALL preserves duplicate rows, which the team ruled out

stem: A bronze column holds values such as 2026-01 as plain strings, and the silver model needs a real date column built from them. The pattern is not one the engine will guess, so the conversion has to be told the layout explicitly.

option_texts.A: to_date on the column alone, since the engine infers any layout it meets
option_texts.B: to_date on the column with a format argument describing the layout
option_texts.C: date_format on the column, which turns a string into a date by pattern
option_texts.D: cast the column to date, which reads any layout the string happens to use

drill_answer_short: to_date(expr, fmt) casts the expression to a date using the supplied formatting
decision_hinge: The to_date function returns expr cast to a date using an optional formatting given by the fmt argument.

plausible_options.A: the silver model needs a real date column built from them

eliminated_by.C: The pattern is not one the engine will guess
eliminated_by.D: the conversion has to be told the layout explicitly

distractor_traps.A: T3: confusable sibling - the bare call works for recognised layouts, which the stem rules out
distractor_traps.C: T2: scope error - date_format renders a date as a string, the opposite direction
distractor_traps.D: T5: common misconception - a plain cast handles standard layouts only

stem: An engineer wants one piece of reusable logic that analysts can call straight from SQL across several notebooks, registered in Unity Catalog so permissions apply to it. Nobody should have to import a helper module to use it.

option_texts.A: CREATE VIEW in the catalog wrapping the logic, which analysts select from instead
option_texts.B: A Python helper in a workspace file that each notebook imports before use
option_texts.C: CREATE FUNCTION, which registers a callable routine in the catalog
option_texts.D: A notebook of shared logic that other notebooks invoke with a run command

drill_answer_short: CREATE FUNCTION registers a SQL or Python user defined function as a catalog object
decision_hinge: The CREATE FUNCTION statement creates a SQL scalar or table function, or a Python scalar function, that takes a set of arguments and returns a value, and the function is registered in the schema where it is created.

plausible_options.A: reusable logic that analysts can call straight from SQL across several notebooks

eliminated_by.B: Nobody should have to import a helper module to use it
eliminated_by.D: registered in Unity Catalog so permissions apply to it

distractor_traps.A: T3: confusable sibling - a view returns a fixed result set and cannot take arguments
distractor_traps.B: T4: breaks a stated requirement - an imported module is exactly what the team ruled out
distractor_traps.D: T2: scope error - a shared notebook is not a governed catalog object

stem: A finance review flags a SQL warehouse that costs money overnight although no analyst queries it after six in the evening. The warehouse is left running so the first morning query does not wait, and the team must explain what the idle hours actually cost.

option_texts.A: An idle warehouse is billed only for the queries it serves, so the hours are free
option_texts.B: An idle warehouse drops to a reduced rate that Auto Stop cannot influence
option_texts.C: An idle warehouse is suspended by the platform automatically after one hour
option_texts.D: An idle warehouse keeps accruing charges until it stops, which Auto Stop controls

drill_answer_short: Idle SQL warehouses continue to accumulate DBU and cloud charges until they stop; Auto Stop sets the idle cut-off
decision_hinge: Auto Stop determines whether the warehouse stops if it is idle for the specified number of minutes, and idle SQL warehouses continue to accumulate DBU and cloud instance charges until they are stopped.

plausible_options.C: The warehouse is left running so the first morning query does not wait

eliminated_by.A: costs money overnight although no analyst queries it
eliminated_by.B: the team must explain what the idle hours actually cost

distractor_traps.A: T5: common misconception - billing follows the running resource, not the query count
distractor_traps.B: T1: fabricated - there is no reduced idle rate for a running warehouse
distractor_traps.C: T3: confusable sibling - stopping is governed by the configured Auto Stop value, not a fixed hour

stem: A team is agreeing what belongs in the middle tier of its medallion design. Analysts want detail preserved for in-depth work, while the aggregated reporting tables are being built separately above it.

option_texts.A: A refined dataset that still retains detailed information for in-depth analysis
option_texts.B: Raw records exactly as they landed, so nothing is lost before processing begins
option_texts.C: Business level aggregates shaped for dashboards rather than in-depth analysis
option_texts.D: A copy of the source system schema kept purely for disaster recovery purposes

drill_answer_short: The Silver layer holds a more refined dataset that still retains the detail needed for in-depth analysis
decision_hinge: Data analysts use the Silver layer for a more refined dataset that still retains detailed information necessary for in-depth analysis.

plausible_options.C: agreeing what belongs in the middle tier of its medallion design

eliminated_by.B: Analysts want detail preserved for in-depth work
eliminated_by.D: the aggregated reporting tables are being built separately above it

distractor_traps.B: T3: confusable sibling - untouched landing records are the Bronze tier, one level below
distractor_traps.C: T3: confusable sibling - business aggregates are the Gold tier, which the stem places above
distractor_traps.D: T1: fabricated - no medallion tier exists for disaster recovery copies

stem: A data quality check has to list the identifiers that appear in an expected set but are absent from the loaded set, using two queries of identical shape. The output must not repeat an identifier even when the expected set holds it twice.

option_texts.A: INTERSECT, which keeps only identifiers found on both of the two sides
option_texts.B: EXCEPT, whose default form returns the first side's rows without duplicates
option_texts.C: EXCEPT ALL, which returns the first side's surplus rows and keeps repeats
option_texts.D: UNION, which brings the two sides together and removes repeated rows

drill_answer_short: EXCEPT returns rows of the first subquery absent from the second, and DISTINCT is the default
decision_hinge: With the set operators, if ALL is specified duplicate rows are preserved, and if DISTINCT is specified the result does not contain any duplicate rows, which is the default.

plausible_options.C: identifiers that appear in an expected set but are absent from the loaded set

eliminated_by.A: using two queries of identical shape
eliminated_by.D: The output must not repeat an identifier

distractor_traps.A: T3: confusable sibling - INTERSECT returns the overlap, the opposite of what is wanted
distractor_traps.C: T3: confusable sibling - ALL preserves the repeats the stem forbids
distractor_traps.D: T5: common misconception - UNION merges the sides instead of subtracting one
